description: Offline-discovered unified-PRM seed rubric set for DSPredict, mined fully bottom-up (no pre-existing rubrics in the loop) from V4-v2 no-PRM DSPredict-Easy trajectories. `grounding` (artifact|trajectory) is an ADVISORY recommendation, not a constraint. Build into RubricDef via dsgym.adapra.rubrics.load_rubrics_from_json.

rubrics.description: Agent fails to maintain a persistent, machine-readable registry of CV scores updated after every experiment, making principled model selection impossible.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent maintains a persistent cv_scores.json (or equivalent) updated after every experiment to enable objective cross-model comparison.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: A machine-readable file (e.g., cv_scores.json) exists in the workspace containing CV scores for every trained model/ensemble, updated consistently throughout the run, and the agent uses it to identify the best model at submission time.
Label 'agent_failure' if: No such registry exists, or it is missing entries for major experiments, or it is overwritten per-run rather than accumulated, preventing reliable comparison across all experiments.
Label 'not_applicable' if: Only a single model was ever trained and no comparison was needed.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The workspace files are not visible and the trajectory does not mention CV score tracking.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Create a cv_scores.json file and append each experiment's name, CV score, std, and metadata immediately after training completes; never overwrite it — always append.
example_evidence: [Turn 63] sorted CV scores printed from cv_scores.json showing stacking_ridge: 0.297996 as best (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_1)
workspace: cv_scores.json lists all 8 experiments with cv_score and cv_std (playground-series-s3e13/attempt_0)
[Turn 427] cv_scores.json was overwritten by each model run so no cumulative comparison was possible (playground-series-s5e4/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to save out-of-fold and test predictions to disk after each model training run, forcing expensive re-training for any ensemble or post-hoc analysis.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent caches OOF and test predictions as parquet files after each model training run to enable fast ensemble search without retraining.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The workspace preds/ directory contains OOF and test prediction files (parquet or similar) for every substantively trained model, and ensemble/stacking scripts load these cached files rather than retraining base models.
Label 'agent_failure' if: No OOF or test prediction files exist for trained models, or ensemble scripts retrain base models from scratch instead of loading cached predictions.
Label 'not_applicable' if: Only a single model was trained and no ensembling was attempted.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The workspace preds/ directory contents cannot be verified from the available information.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: After each CV training loop, save fold-accumulated OOF predictions and test predictions to preds/<model_name>_oof.parquet and preds/<model_name>_test.parquet before proceeding.
example_evidence: workspace: preds/ directory contains oof_lgbm_lgbm_deep.csv, oof_cb_fast.csv — loaded by ensemble script without retraining (house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/attempt_3)
[Turn 12] 'OOF predictions saved to: /workspace/playground-series-s3e13/preds/lgbm_baseline_oof.parquet' (playground-series-s3e13/attempt_0)
workspace: preds/lgbm_baseline_oof.parquet, preds/xgb_baseline_oof.parquet all present, enabling ensemble search in seconds (playground-series-s4e1/attempt_2)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to submit predictions from the model with the highest validated CV score, instead defaulting to the most recently trained model or an overwritten file.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent explicitly selects and submits the model with the best CV score rather than whatever was most recently trained or written to disk.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The final /submission/submission.csv is verifiably sourced from the model/experiment with the highest CV score in the registry, and the agent explicitly checked the registry before writing the final submission.
Label 'agent_failure' if: The submission corresponds to a later, lower-CV experiment that overwrote the best model's output, or the agent selected the most-recent model without checking CV scores.
Label 'not_applicable' if: Only one model was trained so no selection was needed.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: It cannot be determined which model's predictions are in the submission file.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Before finalizing, query cv_scores.json for the best model name, load its cached test parquet file, and write it to /submission/submission.csv — never rely on whatever the last script wrote.
example_evidence: [Turn 71] cp best-CV submission_ensemble_catboost.csv /submission/submission.csv; confirmed by wc -l (house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/attempt_3)

[Turn 106] submission_tuned_logistic_stacking.csv (CV 0.867684) was in /submission/ while best was submission_weighted_ensemble_very_fine.csv (0.867743) — never updated (playground-series-s3e24/attempt_4)
[Turn 128] agent selected MLP (CV 0.512056, worst model) believing higher log-loss was better (playground-series-s3e26/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to verify the final submission file for correct row count, absence of NaN values, valid prediction range, and correct column names before finalizing.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent explicitly verifies submission file integrity (row count, NaN absence, value range, column names) before concluding the attempt.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The trajectory contains an explicit check of the final /submission/submission.csv covering at least row count matching the test set size and absence of NaN values, with results logged.
Label 'agent_failure' if: No integrity check is performed, or the check reveals problems (wrong row count, NaNs, binary corruption, wrong column names) that are not corrected before finishing.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The attempt ended before any submission file was generated.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: It cannot be determined whether a verification step occurred.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: After writing /submission/submission.csv, run: shape check, NaN count, value range, wc -l against expected test size, and column name comparison against sample_submission.csv — fix any issues before calling finish.
example_evidence: [Turn 85] Rows: 240224, NaN values: 0, Min: 50.0, Max: 150.0 — all checks passed (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_1)
[Turn 88] binary parquet copied to submission.csv — binary garbage detected in head output, then fixed (playground-series-s3e9/attempt_4)
[Turn 26] cp stacking_test.parquet submission.csv produced binary file; UnicodeDecodeError caught at Turn 91 (playground-series-s4e5/attempt_1)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to detect when a later experiment has overwritten the submission with worse predictions, or detects it but does not revert to the best-CV model before finishing.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent detects when a subsequent experiment produces a CV regression and explicitly reverts the submission to the best-validated model.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The agent detects (via cv_scores.json comparison or file inspection) that the current submission.csv corresponds to a worse model than a previously computed best, and explicitly restores the best model's predictions to /submission/submission.csv before finishing.
Label 'agent_failure' if: The final submission reflects a worse model because the agent did not check for regressions, or detected a regression but failed to revert before finishing.
Label 'not_applicable' if: Only one model was trained, making regression impossible.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: It cannot be determined whether a regression occurred or was addressed.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: After every experiment that writes to /submission/submission.csv, immediately compare the new CV score to cv_scores.json; if it is not the new best, reload the best model's parquet and rewrite the submission.
example_evidence: [Turn 38] detected stacking LR overwrote submission; reverted to best ensemble predictions (playground-series-s3e13/attempt_0)
[Turn 125] head shows wrong predictions from 4-way-no-hgb; agent restored 5-way-hgb-superfine (playground-series-s3e14/attempt_4)
[Turn 45-48] agent diagnosed leaky calibration as invalid but still copied it to final submission instead of reverting (playground-series-s3e16/attempt_3)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to use a proper held-out cross-validation scheme, instead evaluating models on training data, computing in-sample metrics, or using CV schemes mismatched to the problem type.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent uses a proper out-of-fold or held-out cross-validation scheme that produces honest, unbiased CV score estimates.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: All reported CV scores are computed using held-out fold predictions (OOF) that were not used during model fitting, with an appropriate split strategy for the task (stratified for classification, time-based for time series).
Label 'agent_failure' if: Any CV score in cv_scores.json is computed by evaluating a model on the same data it was trained on (in-sample), or ensemble weights are searched using the same OOF data without a secondary holdout, or the CV scheme is wrong for the task type (e.g., random KFold for time series).
Label 'not_applicable' if: No model training or CV was performed.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The training code is not visible and CV methodology cannot be inferred from outputs.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Ensure every CV score is computed strictly on held-out fold rows the model never saw during fitting; for ensemble weight search, either use a separate holdout or ensure weights are optimized inside the same fold loop that generated OOF predictions.
example_evidence: [Turn 8] train_stacking_meta_v2.py: meta.fit(X_train, y_true) then oof_pred = meta.predict(X_train) — in-sample RMSE 0.029788 recorded as CV (playground-series-s3e15/attempt_4)
[Turn 53] expanding-window CV fold scores [12.52, 9.45, 13.46, 17.46] — early folds dominate mean, misrepresenting true generalization (playground-series-s3e19/attempt_0)
[Turn 143] StratifiedKFold seed=42 used consistently across all model families ensuring comparable CV scores (playground-series-s3e3/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to align the model's training objective with the competition evaluation metric, training on a mismatched loss that systematically biases predictions.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent aligns the model's training objective or target transformation with the competition evaluation metric.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The training loss or target transformation matches the evaluation metric (e.g., log1p target for RMSLE, MAE objective for MedAE, stratified splits for imbalanced AUC, ordinal-aware loss for QWK).
Label 'agent_failure' if: Models are trained with a mismatched objective (e.g., RMSE on raw target for an RMSLE competition, MSE for QWK, no log transform for RMSLE), as evidenced in training scripts or cv_scores.json metadata.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The competition metric is accuracy or AUC and any standard classification objective is acceptable.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Training scripts are not visible and metric alignment cannot be inferred.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: For RMSLE competitions apply log1p to the target and train with RMSE; for QWK use ordinal regression or threshold-optimize continuous predictions; for MedAE use MAE or quantile(0.5) objectives — verify alignment before training any model.
example_evidence: [Turn 47] lgb_params: 'objective': 'regression', 'metric': 'rmse' — no log transform applied despite RMSLE metric (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_0)
train_lgbm_baseline.py: 'objective': 'regression' on raw Rings target despite RMSLE metric (playground-series-s4e4/attempt_0)
cv_scores.json: catboost_v12 uses 'objective': 'MAE' — correctly aligned with MedAE competition metric (playground-series-s3e25/attempt_1)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to train multiple diverse model families or stops at a single model without attempting ensembling, leaving ensemble gains unrealized.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent trains at least two distinct model families and combines them via ensemble or stacking.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The workspace contains trained models from at least two distinct families (e.g., LightGBM + XGBoost, or GBDT + neural net), their OOF predictions are combined via weighted averaging or stacking, and the ensemble CV score is compared against individual models.
Label 'agent_failure' if: Only one model family was trained, or models from multiple families were trained but never combined, or an ensemble was attempted but combined weak+strong models in a way that degraded performance (e.g., blending with a model 2.5pp weaker).
Label 'not_applicable' if: The competition or task type makes single-model submission standard (e.g., data-centric competition where model is fixed).
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Training scripts are not visible.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Train at least LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost; compute pairwise OOF correlation; if correlation < 0.99, run a grid search over blend weights using OOF predictions to find the best ensemble.
example_evidence: cv_scores.json: only 'lightgbm_baseline' entry — no second model attempted (house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/attempt_0)
[Turn 64] CatBoost scored 0.125712 vs prior best 0.126306; blending improved to 0.124118 (house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/attempt_3)
workspace: cv_scores.json: lgbm_baseline=0.8894, xgb=0.8891, catboost=0.8888, ensemble_best_weights=0.8896 (playground-series-s4e1/attempt_2)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to tune model hyperparameters beyond out-of-the-box defaults, submitting with parameters that are known to be suboptimal for the dataset size and task.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent performs at least one principled hyperparameter search beyond default settings for the primary model family.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The workspace contains at least one training script or cv_scores.json entry showing a model trained with non-default hyperparameters (e.g., num_leaves != 31, learning_rate != 0.05, or evidence of a grid/random/Optuna search), and the tuned model's CV score is compared against the baseline.
Label 'agent_failure' if: All models in cv_scores.json use default or near-default hyperparameters (num_leaves=31, max_depth=6, lr=0.05) with no documented search, or a 'tuned' variant was attempted but produced identical CV to the baseline.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The task is data-centric (fixed model) or the competition had a trivially small budget with no time for tuning.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Hyperparameter values are not visible in training scripts or registry.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Run at least a small grid or random search over num_leaves (e.g., [63, 127, 255]) and learning_rate (e.g., [0.03, 0.05, 0.1]) using the CV framework already in place, and record results in cv_scores.json.
example_evidence: workspace: train_lgbm_v2.py — 'num_leaves': 31, 'learning_rate': 0.05, no further tuning; best single model 0.3024 (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_0)
[Turn 104] Best ensemble weights: [0.43, 0.40, 0.17] Best CV Score: 0.561332 after jointly retuning base-model hyperparameters (playground-series-s3e1/attempt_1)
workspace: cv_scores.json shows catboost_tuned cv_mean=0.564775 vs catboost_baseline=0.564821 — no real tuning occurred (playground-series-s3e1/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to diagnose and fix the root cause of a recurring error, instead repeatedly re-running the same crashing code and consuming exploration budget on non-productive debug cycles.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent diagnoses and fixes the root cause of a crash rather than repeatedly re-running the same failing code.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: When a script crashes, the agent identifies the root cause, applies a fix, and the same error does not recur more than once after the fix.
Label 'agent_failure' if: The same error (same exception type and cause, e.g., wrong keyword argument, dtype mismatch, array shape error) appears three or more times across successive turns, indicating the agent is re-running without root-cause diagnosis.
Label 'not_applicable' if: No crashes occurred during the trajectory.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Error messages and fix attempts are not visible in the transcript.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: When a crash recurs after a fix attempt, stop and inspect the full traceback to find the root cause; check library version for API errors (e.g., xgb.early_stop vs callbacks) before re-running.
example_evidence: [Turn 13] TypeError: cv() got unexpected kwarg 'early_stopping_rounds'; [Turn 15] same error after first fix (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_0)
[Turn 26] TypeError: dtype category subtract; [Turn 28] same error repeated (playground-series-s3e16/attempt_3)
[Turn 103] Fixed xgboost API call once definitively, unblocking all downstream experiments (playground-series-s3e1/attempt_1)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to recognize when an experimental axis is saturated and continues running near-identical experiments without CV improvement instead of pivoting to a qualitatively different approach.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent recognizes when an experimental axis has plateaued and pivots to a substantively different approach rather than repeating near-identical experiments.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: After 2-3 consecutive experiments on the same axis (e.g., weight search, seed sweep) produce no meaningful CV improvement (< 0.001 relative), the agent pivots to a different approach (new model family, feature engineering, different stacking architecture).
Label 'agent_failure' if: Five or more consecutive experiments make no substantive change to the modeling approach and produce no meaningful CV improvement, as evidenced by nearly identical cv_scores.json entries or repeated 'No improvement found' outputs.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The agent only ran one or two experiments total.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The number and variety of experiments cannot be determined from the transcript.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: After three consecutive weight-search or seed-sweep experiments with < 0.001 CV gain, stop and try a fundamentally different approach: new model family, richer feature engineering, or a different stacking architecture.
example_evidence: [Turn 96] 'No improvement found. Current best: 0.4978'; [Turn 114] same message — ensemble_weights swept repeatedly (playground-series-s3e13/attempt_4)
[Turn 136] v27 through v40 all output 'Best CV Accuracy: 0.968905' — same script run 14 times with no changes (playground-series-s5e7/attempt_3)
[Turn 30] fine grid search Best CV: 0.867188; [Turn 64] all weight searches within 0.001 AUC after 30+ turns (playground-series-s3e24/attempt_4)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to investigate CV scores that are implausibly better than all other models (indicating data leakage or in-sample evaluation) and either trusts and submits them or notes them without corrective action.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent investigates and correctly handles CV scores that are suspiciously better than all other models (a signal of data leakage or in-sample evaluation).
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: When a model's CV score is substantially better than all others (> 20% relative improvement with no architectural explanation), the agent diagnoses whether it is legitimate or an artifact of leakage/in-sample evaluation, and either discards the model or confirms correctness with a separate holdout before using it for submission.
Label 'agent_failure' if: An obviously inflated CV score (e.g., perfect 1.0 AUC, RMSE 10x better than all others, correlation 0.96 with training labels) is accepted as valid, recorded in cv_scores.json, and used for submission or downstream ensembling without investigation.
Label 'not_applicable' if: No suspiciously anomalous CV scores appeared during the run.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: CV score values are not visible in the trajectory or workspace.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: When a CV score improves by > 20% relative in a single step, immediately check whether the meta-learner was evaluated on its own training data; compute correlation of OOF predictions with true labels — if > 0.9, it is in-sample leakage.
example_evidence: [Turn 36] RF stacking CV 0.029907 flagged as 'too good, likely overfitting' — agent correctly declined to submit (playground-series-s3e15/attempt_1)
workspace: cv_scores.json rank_ensemble: 0.9999999952 — noted as suspicious but never investigated (playground-series-s4e10/attempt_3)
[Turn 26] gbm meta-learner 0.5866 — agent immediately accepted a 10% jump with no investigation and submitted (playground-series-s3e5/attempt_3)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to produce a valid submission file before calling finish, ending the attempt with no scorable entry.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent ensures a valid, complete submission file exists at /submission/submission.csv before concluding the attempt.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: At the time of finish, /submission/submission.csv exists, is a valid CSV with the correct target column and row count matching the test set, and contains non-trivial (non-constant, non-NaN) predictions.
Label 'agent_failure' if: finish is called before any valid submission is written, or the submission file is empty, binary-corrupted, or contains wrong-competition predictions that make it invalid for the actual leaderboard.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The attempt is still in progress and no finish was called.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The submission file contents cannot be verified.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Before calling finish, always run: wc -l /submission/submission.csv to confirm correct row count, and head -3 to confirm correct column names and non-trivial values — if anything is wrong, fix it first.
example_evidence: [Turn 20] ACTION finish called with no submission.csv written — ls /submission shows empty directory (playground-series-s5e5/attempt_0)
[Turn 43] submission contains loan_status float probabilities instead of num_sold sales counts — wrong competition (playground-series-s5e1/attempt_3)
[Turn 88] class distribution: p 2077958, e 6 — essentially constant prediction detected after submission written (playground-series-s4e8/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent applies preprocessing steps that are inappropriate for the model type or task (e.g., StandardScaler before tree models, random KFold for time series, zero-imputation of target values), introducing avoidable noise or computational waste.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent applies preprocessing steps appropriate to the model type and task (avoiding scaling before tree models, using correct imputation, appropriate CV splits).
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: Preprocessing choices are appropriate: no feature scaling before tree-based models, correct imputation strategy for the target distribution, and CV split type matches the task (stratified for imbalanced classification, time-based for time series).
Label 'agent_failure' if: StandardScaler is applied before LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost, target NaN values are imputed with 0 for a forecasting task, or random KFold is used for a time-series problem where temporal leakage would inflate CV scores.
Label 'not_applicable' if: Only linear models were used (where scaling is appropriate) or there were no categorical/missing-value features.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Preprocessing code is not visible.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Remove any StandardScaler from tree-model pipelines; for time-series CV use TimeSeriesSplit or date-based folds; for missing target values use group-mean imputation or row removal rather than zero-fill.
example_evidence: workspace: preprocess.py — StandardScaler applied to all 15 features including binary cols before LGBMRegressor (playground-series-s3e11/attempt_0)
[Turn 53] KFold(shuffle=True) used for time-series forecasting competition — leaks future data into training folds (playground-series-s5e1/attempt_0)
[Turn 18] 'Imputing 8871 missing target values with 0' — biases model for MAPE-evaluated forecasting (playground-series-s5e1/attempt_0)

rubrics.description: Agent launches training jobs without estimating runtime, causing repeated mid-execution kills that produce no usable artifacts and waste the compute budget.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent designs experiments to complete within available time budgets, using prototyping or parameter adjustment rather than launching full training jobs that are repeatedly killed.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: Before launching expensive training jobs (large datasets, many folds, many boosting rounds), the agent either runs a single-fold prototype to estimate runtime, or explicitly limits parameters (sample size, n_folds, n_estimators) to fit within the time budget — and no major training job is killed before saving results.
Label 'agent_failure' if: Two or more training scripts are interrupted with Ctrl-C or timeout before saving any useful predictions or CV scores, indicating the agent launched jobs without verifying they would complete.
Label 'not_applicable' if: All training jobs completed successfully without interruption.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Job runtimes and completion status are not visible in the transcript.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Before a full CV run on large data, time a single fold (timeout 120 python train.py --n_folds 1); if it takes > 60s, reduce sample size, n_estimators, or n_folds to ensure the full run completes within budget.
example_evidence: [Turn 38] timeout 600 python train_catboost.py; [Turn 39] C-c — killed before completion, no artifact saved (playground-series-s3e19/attempt_0)
[Turn 22] C-c interrupting CatBoost; [Turn 31] C-c interrupting CatBoost again — two kills, no CatBoost CV score (playground-series-s4e9/attempt_0)
[Turn 23] single-fold proxy search took 30s per config, agent launched full CV only on best config (playground-series-s5e5/attempt_2)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to invest in domain-relevant feature engineering, submitting with only raw features when known high-value transformations (interaction terms, target encoding, lag features, etc.) are available and appropriate.
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent invests in at least one round of principled feature engineering beyond raw input columns.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: The workspace contains a feature engineering script or module that adds at least 3 non-trivial derived features (interactions, target encodings, lag features, domain-specific transforms), and a CV comparison shows the engineered features improve over raw-feature baseline.
Label 'agent_failure' if: All training scripts use only raw input columns (possibly with label encoding or fillna) and no feature engineering was attempted despite a non-trivial feature space, as evidenced by the feature list or preprocess.py containing no derived columns.
Label 'not_applicable' if: The competition is explicitly data-centric (fixed model) or the feature space is already maximal (e.g., pre-extracted embeddings).
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: Feature engineering code cannot be inspected.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: Create a features.py module with at least: interaction terms between the top-2 most important features, target-encoding for high-cardinality categoricals (computed inside CV folds), and any domain-known transformations (e.g., log for skewed features); validate improvement with CV before committing.
example_evidence: workspace: data.py — extract_date_features creates only calendar columns, no lag or rolling windows for a time-series competition (playground-series-s3e19/attempt_0)
[Turn 24] Mean CV RMSE: 13.0157 with XGBoost + 7 engineered interaction/bin features vs 13.135 baseline (playground-series-s5e4/attempt_1)
[Turn 62] feature ablation: dropping density columns improved CV MedAE from 0.5487 to 0.5262 (playground-series-s3e25/attempt_1)

rubrics.description: Agent fails to detect or investigate obviously impossible or inconsistent CV scores caused by bugs in the metric calculation code (e.g., double log-transformation, wrong target passed).
rubrics.display_description: Whether the agent detects and corrects bugs in metric calculation code before reporting or acting on CV scores.
rubrics.natural_language_instruction:
Label 'agent_success' if: When a CV score appears implausibly low or inconsistent with prior results (e.g., RMSLE of 0.01 when all prior models score ~0.13), the agent identifies and fixes the root cause in the metric code before using the score for model selection.
Label 'agent_failure' if: An obviously buggy metric (double log-transform, wrong target, train-set RMSE) produces a clearly impossible CV score that the agent reports as valid and uses for multiple turns before catching it (if ever).
Label 'not_applicable' if: No metric bugs occurred and all CV scores were plausible.
Label 'insufficient_evidence' if: The metric calculation code is not visible.
rubrics.suggested_actions_hint: After computing a CV score, sanity-check it against competition baselines and prior runs; if it improves by > 30% in a single step with no structural change, print and inspect the raw predictions and targets before proceeding.
example_evidence: [Turn 18] CV Mean: 0.010432 — double log1p bug; agent ran 3 full training passes before catching it at Turn 43 (house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques/attempt_0)
[Turn 129] isotonic calibration with wrong target produced CV 0.1660 — logged as legitimate result (playground-series-s3e13/attempt_4)
[Turn 47] diagnosed OOF initialization bug (np.zeros inflating SMAPE to 50) before using ensemble scores (playground-series-s3e19/attempt_1)
